summary: Retested the two bugs flagged FAIL in iter 5 plus regression sweep. BOTH retest bugs STILL FAIL with the same underlying TypeError. The iter-5 fixes (FileUploader accept-prop parsing + loadInflatedBrain omitting empty layers + handleInflatedToggle guard) only address symptoms — the actual root cause is in niivue calls passing a `name` without a file extension, causing niivue's getFileExt to return undefined and crash. Regression flows (MNI152 load, Clear All, Polar-Angle reload, lesion upload+remove, 3D Render mode) all PASS.

ui_bugs.issue: Inflated LH toggle WITHOUT overlay STILL throws 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading toUpperCase)' inside niivue's getFileExt. Toast 'Failed to load inflated LH · Cannot read properties of undefined (reading toUpperCase)' is shown. Button stays OFF, no mesh in 3D view. Iter-5 fix (omitting layers key) did NOT resolve it.

Tract upload of conte69_lh_inflated.gii STILL throws 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading toUpperCase)' inside niivue's NVMesh.readMesh → getFileExt. No 'Unsupported file format' toast (iter-5 FileUploader fix worked: file passes through), but mesh load itself crashes. Toast: 'Failed to load mesh conte69_lh_inflated.gii · Cannot read properties of undefined (reading toUpperCase)'. No tract entry appears.

action_items: ROOT CAUSE (single bug, two symptoms): niivue 0.68.2 derives the file-extension from the `name` field (NOT the `url` / file.name) when calling `getFileExt`. Both code paths pass an internal id with NO extension:
- loadInflatedBrain: meshSpec = { url: '/atlases/conte69_lh_inflated.gii', name: 'inflated_lh', ... }  -> niivue calls getFileExt('inflated_lh') -> '' -> '.toUpperCase()' on undefined crash.
- addMeshFromFile: NVMesh.loadFromFile({ file, gl, name: 'tract-1700000000000', ... }) -> niivue ignores file.name and uses the provided `name` for ext detection -> crash.
(a) Remove the `name` field from these niivue calls and let niivue infer ext from url/file.name. After load, rename the resulting mesh via `mesh.name = id` (already done in the code).
(b) Keep the id but append the original extension: e.g. `name: `${id}.gii`` for loadInflatedBrain, and ``${id}.${file.name.split('.').pop()}`` for addMeshFromFile.
Option (b) is the smallest diff and least risky.

After patching, re-run both retests; the previously-passing Polar-Angle reload flow works because in that path the OVERLAY layer URL ends in .nii.gz and niivue successfully derives its ext for that layer; the surface mesh load was actually also crashing silently before — verify it now renders.
critical_code_review_comments: Same root cause affects BOTH bugs — a single targeted fix in NiivueViewer.jsx (lines 296-302 for addMeshFromFile and lines 331-345 for loadInflatedBrain) resolves both.
Iter-5's FileUploader allowlist fix is correct and working (no false 'Unsupported file format' toast for .gii now).

Iter-5's handleInflatedToggle guard (only flip state on non-null mesh) is correct and working — that's why button correctly stays OFF on crash. But this hides the bug from the user; consider also surfacing toast.error (already done).
loadInflatedBrain omitting layers when no overlay is correct hygiene but did NOT fix the crash — the crash is in mesh URL parsing, not the layers array.

rca_of_the_issue: niivue 0.68.2 internal helper getFileExt(name) calls name.split('.').pop().toUpperCase(). When the caller passes a custom `name` field without a dot (e.g. 'inflated_lh' or 'tract-1700000000000'), split('.').pop() returns the same string, then .toUpperCase() works — BUT niivue checks `if (!ext) return ''` differently per branch; in NVMesh.readMesh path the `ext` is taken from a different variable that ends up undefined when name has no dot, hence the crash. Reproduction: Click toggle-inflated-lh on a fresh load (RETINOTOPY default 'surface only'). Console immediately logs: loadInflatedBrain failed: TypeError ... at getFileExt. Same for upload of any .gii via tract uploader. Mitigation: ensure `name` passed to niivue has a recognised extension OR remove `name` from the initial load call and rename mesh afterwards via mesh.name = id.
